_meta.description: Indicative coverage status for quantum-related scenarios under typical cyber insurance policies. No insurer or market body has published a quantum-specific exclusion that this model could find, so every cell is 'ambiguous': the outcome turns on general cyber wording, in particular whether cyber cover is affirmed or excluded, and whether an attack attributed to a state falls under a state-backed cyber-attack exclusion.
sources: Lloyd's Market Bulletin Y5258 — Providing clarity for Lloyd's customers on coverage for cyber exposures (2019): policies must affirm or exclude cyber cover (https://assets.lloyds.com/assets/y5258-providing-clarity-for-lloyd-s-customers-on-coverage-for-cyber-exposures/1/Y5258%20-%20Providing%20clarity%20for%20Lloyd%E2%80%99s%20customers%20on%20coverage%20for%20cyber%20exposures.pdf)

Lloyd's Market Bulletin Y5381 — Cyber-attack exclusions (17 August 2022): standalone cyber policies must exclude losses from state-backed cyber-attacks from 31 March 2023 (https://assets.lloyds.com/media/e9a4058c-4c25-48d6-99d3-0c466987e099/Y5381%20Market%20Bulletin%20-%20Cyber-attack%20exclusions.pdf)

coverageValues.covered: Typically covered under standard cyber policy language
coverageValues.excluded: Explicitly excluded by policy wording, for example a state-backed cyber-attack or war exclusion
coverageValues.ambiguous: Coverage unclear — policy wording does not specifically address quantum-origin attacks; subject to dispute at claims time

_meta.note: Educational model — actual coverage depends on specific policy wording. Consult a licensed insurance professional.
